formHint: Uses the connection's saved data (not the unsaved changes in the form).
title: Copy connection string
placeholderHint: A placeholder such as ${DB_PASSWORD} goes in its place, for you to replace.
passwordPrompt: The connection “{{connection}}” doesn't save its password. Enter the password for {{user}} to put it in the string (it isn't saved):
copiedSecret: Copied (includes the password). If it is still on the clipboard, it is cleared in 60 seconds.

blocked.vault_db: Temporary HashiCorp Vault credentials are not copied: DBine revokes them on disconnect.
blocked.iam: The password is a temporary IAM token: it is not copied.

note.tunnel: This connection uses an SSH tunnel ({{ssh}}): the string points to the server; from another machine you need the same tunnel.
note.iam: Uses an IAM token: the password is temporary. DBine generates it when connecting; your application has to generate its own (${DB_IAM_TOKEN}).
note.vault_db: The credentials come from HashiCorp Vault and are temporary: your application has to request its own from Vault.
note.secret_manager: The password comes from a secret manager: with “Include password” it is read from there when copying.
note.password_not_saved: The connection doesn't save its password: with “Include password” it is requested when copying.
note.tls_unverified: The connection trusts the server certificate: the string encrypts but does not verify the certificate.
note.odbc_driver_name: The ODBC driver name ({{driver}}) must match the one installed on the machine where it is used.
note.odbc_clients: The same string works for pyodbc, System.Data.Odbc, node-odbc and any ODBC client.
note.odbc_extra: The connection's additional ODBC attributes are not copied (they may contain credentials): add the ones you need.
note.saved_string: This connection uses an ODBC string saved as a secret: with “Include password” it is copied as is.
note.saved_string_mongo: If the connection uses a connection string saved as a secret, with “Include password” it is copied as is.
note.same_uri: The same URI works for the official Node.js, Python, Java, Go and .NET drivers.
note.stackexchange_commas: StackExchange.Redis does not allow commas in the password of this string.
note.keyspaces: Amazon Keyspaces requires TLS with the Amazon certificate and service-specific credentials.
note.credentials_apart: This format has no user or password: the client receives them separately.
note.neptune_iam: Neptune with IAM signs every connection with SigV4: the driver needs the AWS authentication plugin.
note.token_apart: The token is not in the URL: the client receives it separately (in the Node.js configuration it is included).
note.jdbc_properties: The URL is on the first line; user and password are properties of the JDBC connection.
note.jdbc_role: To connect as {{role}}, add the property internal_logon={{role}}.
note.wallet: The database wallet is needed on the machine where it is used ({{dir}}).
note.tns_alias: It is a TNS alias from the wallet: the machine where it is used needs its tnsnames.ora (TNS_ADMIN).
note.access_token: Signs in with a Microsoft Entra ID access token: your application has to obtain it and pass it separately (AccessToken).
note.integrated: Windows integrated authentication: it has no user or password and uses the session of whoever runs the application.
note.ntlm: NTLM sign-in: the user is written as DOMAIN\user.
note.entra: Signs in with Microsoft Entra ID: it has no password, the client library obtains it.
note.node_integrated: tedious has no Windows integrated authentication: use msnodesqlv8 or a SQL Server user.
note.go_azuread: With fedauth, go-mssqldb uses the “azuresql” driver (azuread package).
note.cosmos_database: The database ({{database}}) is chosen in code, not in the string.
note.aws_profile: Uses the AWS profile “{{profile}}”: the SDK reads it from ~/.aws (or from AWS_PROFILE).
note.aws_default: Uses the default AWS credentials (environment variables, ~/.aws, instance role).
note.gcp_service_account: Uses a Google Cloud service account: set the path of the JSON file in GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS.
note.gcp_adc: Uses the default Google Cloud credentials (gcloud auth application-default login).
note.emulator: The connection points to an emulator: set its address in the client (SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST).
note.keypair: Signs in with a key pair: save the key in a file and set its path in ${PRIVATE_KEY_FILE}.
note.pat: The password is the connection's programmatic access token (PAT).
note.databricks_pat: The connection signs in with OAuth or a service principal: the string uses a personal access token instead.
note.other_port: This format uses the server's port {{port}}, not the one DBine uses: change it if yours is different.
note.files_folder: It is a folder of files: open them from the application with DuckDB (read_csv, read_parquet…).
